hook_text: Some of the oldest arrows in the world may come from a cave in KwaZulu-Natal.
clip_script: KwaDukuza, a museum display. Tiny stone points, each smaller than a fingernail, from Sibudu Cave. Some scientists think they tipped arrows sixty thousand years ago or more. Before the bow, hunters had to get close with spears. The bow and arrow changed everything: shoot from far away, safely hidden. San bows were small, arrows were light reeds with bone heads, and the poison did the work. Then the trackers followed, and the meat was shared.
visual_style: Whiteboard close-up of tiny stone points, then a small bow drawing back, an arrow flying, and footprints leading across the sand.
mood: Clever and exciting, like discovering an ancient invention.
pacing: Slow close-up on the points, quick arrow flight, then a patient tracking trail.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and explain to a friend why the poison mattered more than the bow.
